Nablawave is an advanced engineering company providing R&D services in the Aerospace, Energy and Turbomachinery sectors. We follow new projects from the preliminary design phase to experimental tests, suggesting a mixed approach able to minimise development time and costs.

Nablawave strongly believes in technology contamination: new ideas and concepts coming from traditional industries can bring relevant advantages to the Aerospace sector providing smart, cost-effective solutions. Our expertise can be valuable on several points: 
1.	We know how to decrease space propulsion development costs by widely adopting commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components. Often small variations on the propulsion system layout can have large impacts on development, safety, operational costs, as well as time to market.
2.	We know how to assess propulsion concepts in the most efficient way: a mix of design, numerical simulation, and testing, that permits to strongly reduce the development time. 
3.	We know how to exploit experimental facilities, increasing the number of tests per day and reducing testing costs. In our experience it is possible to design, build, and organize flexible and fast testing facilities with low budgets, respecting safety requirements. Our team successfully designed and tested different lab-scale rocket engines (from less than 1 kN up to 10 kN). We carried out more than 500 tests on different propulsion system configurations using a lot of COTS and industrial equipment. 

At the heart of Nablawave there is a team of passionate professionals (researchers, engineers, Ph.Ds) with transversal skills, capable of providing simple and unique solutions. Optimization algorithms and machine learning are seamlessly integrated with advanced analysis and design tools to handle the most complex modelling problems; the result is a drastic acceleration of the R&D process and an important reduction in costs. Our services include:
-	Mechanical design 
-	Structural, fluid-dynamic, vibro-acoustic simulations, combustion and fluid-structure interaction; all the simulations can be coupled with our in-house optimization software 
-	Development of tailor-made engineering software and algorithms, digital twins, optimization and machine learning 
-	Assistance with experimental testing

entityDescription: The National Observatory of Athens (NOA) is a national organization operating under public law rules and procedures and is supervised by the appropriate Directorate of the General Secretariat for Research and Technology of the Ministry of Development. It is financed through the State Budget of the Ministry of Development. In addition, NOA secures funds from services to other ministries and private parties and from research funds of the open programs of the various Directorates of the European Commission and the Community Structural Fund. The mission of NOA is stated to be ¡the observation, the collection of relevant data and the research of the stellar and solar space, the atmospheric environment, the crust and the interior of the earth�. entityDescription:
Heureka, the Finnish Science Centre introduces the public to science and technology in an engaging and interactive way. Visitors can experience the joy of discovery through spectacular exhibitions, planetarium films, educational programmes and events.
Located in the Tikkurila area of Vantaa, Heureka first opened its doors to the public in 1989. Heureka is one of Finland’s most popular recreational centres, attracting an average of nearly 300,000 visitors each year. Heureka’s operations are subsidized by the Ministry of Education and Culture and the City of Vantaa.

Heureka's history
The roots of Heureka, the Finnish Science Centre can be traced back to the University of Helsinki and scientists, who had become acquainted with different science centres located around the world. The initial spark was lit by Adjunct Professors Tapio Markkanen, Hannu I. Miettinen and Heikki Oja.
It all began with the Physics 82 exhibition held at the House of the Estates in Helsinki on 20–26 May 1982. During autumn of that same year, the science centre project was launched with the initial support of the Academy of Finland, the Ministry of Education, and various foundations. The project led to the establishment of the Finnish Science Centre Foundation during 1983-1984. The original founding members of the foundation included the University of Helsinki, the Helsinki University of Technology, the Federation of Finnish Learned Societies, and the Confederation of Industries.
In 1984, the City of Vantaa offered to be the host city and partial financier for the Science Centre, and also designated a property lot located in the southern end of Tikkurila as the future site of the centre. An architectural competition, held in 1985, turned out two first prizes from which the winning design was selected; namely the “Heureka” design submitted by Mikko Heikkinen, Markku Komonen and Lauri Anttila. That’s how the Finnish Science Centre Heureka got its apt name!
Before the building was completed, a number of test exhibitions were set up at other sites. The interior plan for the Science Centre was completed in 1986. The foundation for the building was laid in October 1987, and the construction work was completed one year later. The overall area of the building is 8,200 m², of which 2,500 m² is exhibition space. The Finnish Science Centre Heureka opened its doors to the public on 28 April 1989.

In former days, Space Systems Czech (SSC) was established in Czech Republic as a sister company of Space Systems Finland (SSF) fully adopting its culture, practices and quality standards. Qfluidics is a young French startup developing its breakthrough “liquid tube” technology. In short, we use magnetic liquids to transport other liquids. Our technology allows us to transport various fluids without any solid contact granting unique advantages over conventional pumping/valving technologies: 
• Abrasive insensitivity (to transport slurries without damaging the pump) 
• Up to 99% pressure drop reduction (very useful to transport viscous fluids at a low energy cost) 
• A very soft pumping action (low-shear) to transport fragile biological fluids (cells, whole blood, etc.)

At the moment, Qfluidics is focused on collaborative projects to introduce and adapt its liquid tube technology to solve issues of various industries.

Eurecat (www.eurecat.org) is the leading technology centre in Catalonia and the second largest private research organisation in southern Europe.
Eurecat furnishes the business and industrial sector with unique technology and advanced knowledge to address the innovation needs of companies and make them more competitive. The added value provided by Eurecat fast-tracks innovation, cuts outlay on scientific and technological infrastructures, minimises risks and delivers specialised expertise tailored to each company’s requirements. It brings standout solutions to unlock the value chain with initiatives which leverage innovation and business to build capabilities, streamline resources and drive profitability. 
Eurecat is also committed to working with other players in the domestic innovation system. It has partnership agreements in place with other centres which enable technology research and development calling for skills and teams available at other facilities to be conducted jointly and cost-effectively for businesses. We are a member of 22 technology platforms, 12 Digital Innovation Hubs and 37 European associations.
As part of its global outlook Eurecat pursues an internationalisation strategy anchored in three key objectives: supporting companies in their expansion abroad through technological innovation, driving cross-border strategic partnerships and marketing its product and services portfolio.

Workforce: > 650
Parity (W/M): 42%/58%
Customers: > 1.700
Patents: 153
Annual income: 49,2 million euros
Sites: 11
Spin-offs: 8
Consortium R&D projects: 200+
Ongoing H2020 projects led: 33
Ongoing H2020 projects: 86

Taken together these areas have extensive knowhow and expertise in over 20 scientific and technological fields including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, advanced manufacturing, smart materials, printed electronics, robotics and automation, medical devices, circular economy, climate change and nutrition and health.
These multi-technology and multidisciplinary capabilities enable Eurecat to systematically address complex challenges as a world-class partner for businesses in domains such as Industry 4.0, the digital transformation of production sectors, the circular economy, smart cities, personalised nutrition, predictive medicine and the digital economy. It also has state-of-the-art scientific and technological facilities and laboratories including its Omic Sciences Centre, its Plastronics pilot plant which is a groundbreaker in Europe, and its regional 3D manufacturing laboratory network.
Eurecat’s operations target a range of key business sectors which are significant due to their footprint in the region and their contribution to its GDP. CYENS CoE is the Research Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Cyprus in the area of Information and Communication Technologies focusing on Interactive media, Smart systems and Emerging technologies. The Centre of Excellence fosters world-class research activities and at the same time aims to serve as a paradigm for bridging scientific research with innovation outside academia. It is a joint venture between the three public universities of Cyprus (University of Cyprus, Cyprus University of Technology, Open University of Cyprus), the Municipality of Nicosia, and two renowned international partners, the Max Planck Institute for Informatics (Germany) and University College London (UK).

CYENS CoE is designed to act as an integrator of academic research and innovation, towards the sustainable fuelling of scientific, technological and economic growth of Cyprus and Europe, empowering knowledge and technology transfer in the region.
 
CYENS CoE consists of three Research Pillars (RP) representing the three main research areas of Visual Sciences, Human Factors and Design, and Communication and Artificial Intelligence:
· The RP of Visual Sciences: includes the research areas of Computer Graphics, Computer Vision, Imaging and Virtual/Augmented Reality. 
· The RP of Human Factors and Design: includes the research areas of human-computer interaction, applied perception and cognition.
· The RP Communication and Artificial Intelligence: incorporates the research areas of machine learning models, cognitive models of natural language, psychological models of attention, common sense reasoning, analysis of interaction in social networks, distributed/networked systems, mechanisms for ensuring multimedia application support, controlled network performance and quality of experience, and the integration of embedded systems and sensors in the data stream.
Sixteen multidisciplinary innovation-driven research groups (MRG’s) accommodate more than 60 research staff of CYENS CoE.

State of the art facilities and equipment is available for big data and deep learning, computer vision, augmented and virtual reality and computer graphics, amongst others, as well as a fully functional creative space. The creative space equipped with fabrication, rapid prototyping, electronics, Mix-R and machining laboratory offers researchers, entrepreneurs and any other interested party, opportunities to transform, to share, test and perfect their ideas.

Institute of Educational Policy (IEP) was established in 2011 under Public Law 3966 (Government Gazette Α’ 118/24-05-2011). It is a Public Entity under Private Law supervised by the Ministry of Education and Religious Affairs. IEP operates for the benefit of public interest as an executive scientific body that supports the Ministry of Education and Religious Affairs on issues related to primary and secondary education as well as the transition from secondary to higher education. IEP is also responsible for the in-service teacher training, the formal curriculum development, the educational material as well as the assessment tools used at national level. IEP’s primary mission is the scientific research and study of issues related to all levels of education, the contribution to the design and implementation of educational policy issues and the implementation of co-funded projects. According to Law 4763/2020 (Government Gazette A’ 254/21-12-2020), there are three Scientific Departments:
· Department A: Educational Innovation and Inclusive Education
· Department B: School Curricula and Educational material
· Department C: In-service training & Evaluation, European and International Educational Policy.
Moreover, the Department of Projects and Actions is responsible for coordinating IEP participation, either as project coordinator or partner, in both Partnership Agreement 2014-2020 and EU (co)funded programmes (Erasmus+ etc).
